messages:
rachel: Quick question from yesterday's cross-country flight. I bought in-flight Wi-Fi to join a customer call ($12). I also paid $45 to upgrade to extra-legroom seat at checkout. I used my personal card because the company card hit the daily limit. What attachments do you need and are these reimbursable? cc @travel-admin

travel-admin: Short answer: Wi-Fi = reimbursable when used for work; seat upgrades = conditional. Need receipts/proof and manager OK for the upgrade if over policy thresholds.

travel-admin: For Wi-Fi: upload the provider receipt (in-app or email) or a screenshot of the connection confirmation that shows the charge, plus the card statement line. If the purchase appears as a bundled item on the airline receipt (e.g., "Wi-Fi bundle"), that's fine too.

travel-admin: For seat/upgrade: policy default reimburses standard economy fares only. Extra-legroom or preferred-economy upgrades are reimbursable up to $50 for flights >3 hours with manager approval. Premium-economy, lie-flat business, and first-class upgrades require pre-approval from manager + People Ops for the cost above the standard fare.

rachel: I didn't get pre-approval (my bad). The upgrade was $45, under $50. I have the airline receipt showing the seat charge and my bank txn. Will manager approval after-the-fact be OK?

travel-admin: If it's under the per-trip informal cap ($50) and you document it, we can approve post-hoc. Add a note in the expense: "work call + long flight; extra-legroom to take notes on customer call" and ask your manager to acknowledge in the expense comments. If your manager is fine, finance will clear it.

tom: Related: what if I used frequent-flyer miles to upgrade and paid only taxes/fees on my card? Can I claim those taxes/fees?

travel-admin: Yes. When upgrades are purchased with miles, reimbursable items are the out-of-pocket taxes/fees you paid on your card (attach boarding pass/itinerary showing class change + card stmt showing tax/fee). We do not reimburse the value of miles.

rachel: And if the company card had been used (instead of personal), is approval still required?

travel-admin: Company card purchases for upgrades still follow policy. If the card pays for a small extra-legroom fee <=$50 and manager signs off, OK. If merchant posts a large premium upgrade charge, People Ops needs to sign off before booking. Use the company card only for approved business-eligible upgrades.

travel-admin: Also: if the upgrade was refundable and you later cancelled, include the refund evidence. We will not reimburse a charge that was refunded to you personally. If the refund went to the company card, finance will reconcile.

people-ops: Policy snippet:
```
- In-flight connectivity: reimbursable when used for business. Attach provider receipt/screenshot + card txn. Cap: $25 per long-haul leg unless pre-approved.
- Seat upgrades: reimbursable for extra-legroom/priority seats up to $50 with manager approval. Premium-economy/business/first require pre-approval from manager + People Ops.
- Miles-based upgrades: reimburse taxes/fees only; miles are non-reimbursable.
- Use company card when available; if personal card used, explain why and attach card stmt.
```

finance-bot: Reminder: any single item > $75 requires explicit manager approval in the expense comments. Missing approval may trigger an audit hold.

rachel: Thanks. I uploaded the airline receipt with the seat line and the Wi-Fi confirmation, plus the bank txn. I also pinged my manager for a quick approval in the expense comments.

tom: One edge case: on a multi-leg itinerary the extra-legroom fee applied only to the domestic leg. Can we reimburse just that leg's upgrade?

travel-admin: Yes, reimburse per-leg charges. Attach the itinerary showing which segment got upgraded and the vendor receipt showing the charge per segment. If you used miles for one leg and paid for another, follow the miles vs fees rule.

rachel: Great — manager approved in the comments. Thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:

travel-admin: We'll clear it in the next run. Finance may ask for the manager's Slack confirmation to attach to the expense if the approval was verbal.

finance-bot: Process note: upload receipts with clear merchant names, show last 4 digits on the card statement, and include a one-line justification when purchasing upgrades or connectivity.
